summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Arqos Systems through Optimize quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8). Focus on quality vs latency tradeoffs, recommended profiles for their chat summarization workload, and next steps to run benchmarks and share security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-20 15:00 PST | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Evan Park, Maya Singh (Redwood) — Jordan Lee, Priya Natarajan, Carlos Ruiz (Arqos)

[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is Evan from Redwood, AE on the account, and Maya is our systems SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Jordan: Good, thanks. Excited to see the optimize walkthrough — we want to understand INT8 vs FP8 for our summarization pipeline.
[00:20] Maya: Great. quick agenda: show the Optimize UI, walk through quantization profiles, share quality vs latency charts, then talk pilot/next steps. we'll try to keep it interactive.
[00:35] Carlos: Sounds good. main constraints: sub-200ms p99 for short chat completions, and cost has to be materially lower than our current hosted spend.
[00:48] Priya: plus we need EU data residency and SOC2 evidence for the pilot.
[00:54] Evan: yeah totally — we'll cover Dedicated vs Private briefly and call out the security pack.

[01:15] Maya: Ok jumping into the Optimize console — you can see quant profiles on the left, we pre-define INT8, FP8 and mixed profiles. for your workload our baseline is FP16 -> gives highest quality but higher latency/cost. INT8 cuts model size and compute, FP8 sits in between.
[01:40] Jordan: quick question: FP8 is stable on all backends? we run both A100 and some newer L4-like instances.
[01:50] Maya: FP8 support depends on kernel and runtime; on our managed hosted fleet FP8 is available for supported models and GPUs, and on Dedicated we can enable it if the hardware/driver stack supports it. there are cases where FP8 gains are better on e.g., H100-class chips. small transcription note: sometimes our notes say 'H-100' or 'Hone' in the transcript, ignore that.

[02:20] Maya: showing a quality vs latency scatter — y axis is ROUGE/accuracy deltas vs baseline FP16, x axis is median latency. for your summarization model, INT8 typically reduces latency by ~30-45% with a 1-3% drop in ROUGE at typical prompt lengths; FP8 gives ~15-25% latency reduction and <1% quality delta in many cases.
[02:55] Priya: that 1-3% ROUGE loss in INT8 is acceptable if we can tune prompts, right?
[03:06] Maya: Yes, and Optimize can create per-text evals and produce regression alerts. we can also roll out a canary on a fraction of traffic for validation.

[03:35] Jordan: numbers — what does that translate to cost per 1M tokens? we need to compare to our current vendor.
[03:42] Evan: rough back-of-envelope — switching to INT8 can be 35-50% cheaper on token compute cost depending on batching and caching. we should run a workload-specific benchmark to get exact numbers.
[03:58] Carlos: do you do KV cache / prefix caching? we are very chatty with long contexts.
[04:05] Maya: yes we support KV cache and prefix caching; Optimize recommends cache policies. note: sometimes notes will read 'K V cash' in the transcript, sorry for the auto transcription. caching reduces repeated token cost substantially for long chat sessions.

[04:35] Jordan: on the security side — can we get KMS integration and audit logs for Private?
[04:42] Evan: absolutely. Private has customer-managed KMS/HSM and full audit logs; Dedicated includes RBAC and optional VPC peering. we'll attach SOC2 and ISO docs to the follow-up.

[05:05] Priya: are there known model quality regressions with FP8 on summarization tasks?
[05:12] Maya: FP8 tends to be safe for many transformer decoders when quantization-aware calibration is applied. the risk is lower than INT8 generally, but edge cases exist — e.g., numeric precision in extraction tasks. that's why we do evals across your golden set.

[06:00] Evan: let's talk about deployment choices: Hosted API gets you fastest time-to-value. Dedicated reserved offers predictable throughput and burst capacity. Private if you need on-prem or strict data residency. for the pilot we often recommend Hosted or Dedicated depending on contract.
[06:25] Jordan: we'd prefer Dedicated for predictability but may start on Hosted for quick validation.

[06:40] Maya: demoing the Optimize bench tool — you can upload a sample corpus; it runs both INT8 and FP8 profiles across models, returns latency percentiles, cost estimates, and quality diffs. I'm starting a run now with sample prompts you provided earlier (we're using a 500-sample subset).
[07:05] [screen share noise] Maya: run kicked off — ETA ~20 minutes for this subset. It will produce ROUGE, BLEU, and latency p50/p95/p99.

[07:30] Carlos: can we set custom SLOs? like p99 < 200ms?
[07:37] Maya: Yep set SLOs in the console and Optimize will flag regressions and suggest different batching/quant profiles.

[08:00] Jordan: competitor question — if we move to Redwood do we lose multi-model flexibility? we need to run some in-house models and some open-source ones.
[08:10] Evan: you can bring-your-own-model on Dedicated and Private; Hosted has curated catalog but we can support custom model onboarding. we'll note that for the pilot.

[08:35] Priya: what's the suggested fallback policy if INT8 produces bad outputs for some customers?
[08:42] Maya: automatic fallback to FP8 or FP16 per policy; Optimize can route by route or user tier. the rollout (canary/A-B) is configurable in Console.

[09:10] Jordan: any gotchas around prompt engineering when quantized?
[09:18] Maya: sometimes deterministic tokenization or more explicit system prompts help, and we recommend adding a small calibration set to fine-tune the profile. not real fine-tuning but light calibration of decoding params.

[09:45] [09:45] Maya: a note in the transcript — 'throughput onion' instead of 'throughput tuning' — ignore the mis-transcribe.

[10:10] Maya: sharing partial results from the 500-sample run — FP8 results (median latency 98ms, p99 170ms) quality delta vs FP16: -0.4% ROUGE; INT8 (median 62ms, p99 120ms) quality delta: -2.5% ROUGE. cost delta: INT8 ~45% lower compute cost vs FP16, FP8 ~25% lower.
[10:40] Carlos: p99 120ms for INT8 is great. we need to validate on full dataset.

[11:05] Evan: action item — Maya will run a longer 1k sample run with your exact prompts and provide a spreadsheet with per-prompt diffs and failure cases. Evan will also send pricing grid for Hosted vs Dedicated for INT8/FP8.

[11:35] Priya: on compliance please include our legal and security folks in the next thread — they'll want SOC2 plus encryption-at-rest details.
[11:44] Evan: will do.

[12:05] Jordan: curious about quantization profiles per model family — do you have presets?
[12:12] Maya: yes presets by model architecture and use-case — e.g., chat vs summarization vs token-classification. Optimize recommends profile and you can tweak quantization bits, per-channel vs per-tensor, and calibration params.

[12:45] Carlos: is FP8 safe for math or code-gen tasks? we do occasional code summarization.
[12:52] Maya: code-gen is more sensitive; FP8 can be ok but we'd typically favor FP16 or FP8 with conservative calibration. for numeric-heavy tasks we caution to validate thoroughly.

[13:20] [13:20] Maya: demoing the 'quality vs latency' matrix in Optimize — you can filter by p99 and by quality threshold. set your threshold and it shows recommended profile and expected cost.

[13:53] Jordan: latency targets: our internal threshold is 200ms p99 for live chat. can you get p99 <200 for our profiles?
[13:59] Maya: in our sample run yes — INT8 p99 120ms, FP8 p99 170ms. with KV caching and batching some calls will be lower. but real-world results depend on prompt length distribution and concurrency.

[14:30] Carlos: what's the ramp timeline for Dedicated if we decide to go that route?
[14:36] Evan: typically 4-6 weeks for provisioning, optionally faster if we have committed capacity. pilot on Hosted can start within days.

[15:00] Priya: what's included in the pilot SLA?
[15:06] Evan: pilot typically uses best-effort SLAs; Dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for contractual deals. we'll share the SLA doc.

[15:30] [15:30] Maya: a quick note about mixed precision — some teams run mixed FP8/INT8 where critical layers remain higher precision; that gets you most gains with minimal quality impact. it's a good middle ground.

[16:05] Jordan: for the benchmark spreadsheet — can you include columns for prompt length, tokens, model variant, quant profile, p50/p95/p99 latency, and per-prompt quality diff?
[16:14] Maya: yep will include that exact schema.

[16:35] Evan: competitor angle — you mentioned vendor X (OpenAI) and Y (Anthropic), difference here is we give you direct control over quant profiles and can run on Dedicated/private with KMS. you won't be locked into a single model.

[17:00] Carlos: pricing question again — how granular is billing if we do mixed profiles?
[17:07] Evan: billing is by token compute and model route; Optimize returns estimated per-token cost by profile so you can project costs for mixed deployments.

[17:30] Priya: any additional compliance artifacts we should expect?
[17:36] Evan: SOC2, ISO summary, data-flow diagrams, encryption docs — we'll attach these to the follow-up.

[18:05] Maya: sharing some failure-case examples from other customers — INT8 sometimes drops on edge-case entity extraction, and FP8 helped. we can flag those via automated evals.

[18:40] Jordan: what about model rollbacks? if we see regression, is there an easy rollback?
[18:46] Maya: yes built-in canary and automatic rollback policy. you can tie it to quality thresholds.

[19:10] Evan: wrapping: next steps recap — Evan send pricing & security docs; Maya run 1k benchmark and share spreadsheet; Jordan provide sample prompts and latency SLOs. we'll aim to reconvene after Arqos reviews the benchmark.

[19:40] Jordan: thanks everyone. any other Qs?

[19:44] Carlos: not from me.

[19:46] Priya: please cc security@arqos on the docs.

[19:49] Evan: will do.

[20:00] [end of recording — note the meeting lasted ~52 minutes; some timestamps have been rounded and transcription contains minor errors and misheards (e.g., 'K V cash' for KV cache, 'H-100' for H100). Full benchmark and docs to follow via email.]
